title: Local model through a vendor CLI
lead: *Proposed:* let a role run on the owner's local vLLM server (qwen3.8-27b) through the vendor CLIs ork already spawns, with no new HTTP client and no new dependency. No adj record decides this yet.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
- The local server speaks OpenAI Chat Completions, OpenAI Responses and Anthropic Messages, so `claude`, `codex` and `grok` can each be pointed at it. It costs nothing per token, has no external rate limit, keeps code on the owner's hardware, and works with no AI provider reachable.
- Limits (owner-stated, not measured here): much weaker than frontier models; slower per request (tens of seconds); about 2 to 4 concurrent requests (owner estimate); one model served at a time; no SLA.
- The `-local` wrappers (`claude-local`, `codex-local`, `grok-local`) are shell functions and config files in the sibling repo (`agents/llmnode/docs/agents.md:22-60`). A headless spawn by ork does not run a shell function. Their source is not in any repo (`agents/llmnode/open-questions.md:33`).
- ork maps only `claude code`, `codex` and `grok` to an adapter (`internal/daemon/runs.go:349`). Matrix row r33 (Agent `Local (vLLM)`, qwen3.8-27b) is added as a candidate and stays "skipped: no adapter" until this slice decides how a local row maps.
- Owner guidance, a judgment and not measured: local suits mechanical edits from a clear spec, test and doc generation for existing code, log and diff summaries, private code, long unattended loops and offline use. Frontier suits planning, hard debugging, large refactors, unfamiliar code and review of local output. Pattern: plan with frontier, execute with local, review with frontier.
- Candidate models, not in the matrix: Qwen3.8-27B 8-bit (listed by vllm-metal, untested); Nemotron 3.5 Lightning 30B-A3B 4-bit (experimental on vllm-metal, untested). Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B is not available locally.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
Tests use the existing fake vendor scripts; no live server.

- A matrix row with Agent `claude-local` or `codex-local` gives a lineup entry whose vendor is that name; `ork roles matrix` prints `used as claude-local`. A Grok row whose model is the configured local Grok model gives vendor `grok-local`.
- `supportsVendor` accepts the three local vendors; `vendors set` can mark one out.
- The dispatcher runs the claude adapter with binary `claude-local` (and codex with `codex-local`), and passes no base URL or key.
- A cloud `claude` out mark does not skip a `claude-local` entry, and the reverse.
- The local cap of 2 holds across the three local vendors together; a third local role waits for a slot.
- A launcher that exits with the unreachable-endpoint output falls back to the next matrix row; a denied or unclassified exit still stops for the owner (adj 156).
- A row with no launcher on PATH is skipped with a reason naming the launcher, and does not fail the run.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
Owner decisions of 2026-11-06 (this session, answered interactively; not yet recorded in adj): cover claude, codex and grok; `claude-local` and `codex-local` are executables on PATH; Grok has the local model in its regular config, so there is no separate launcher; local rows get their own vendor identity, out mark and slot cap; the cap is 2; no role defaults to local; fallback to the next cloud row is automatic when the endpoint is unreachable; one local model at a time.

1. Verify first, on the owner's machine, and record each command and result: `command -v claude-local codex-local` in the environment the daemon starts with; each launcher run headless with the flags ork passes (`--effort`, `-m`, resume) against the server; the exact model name of the local entry in Grok's config. Do not assume. If a launcher is only an alias or function, stop and ask.
2. Mapping: Agent `claude-local` maps to the claude adapter with binary `claude-local` and lineup vendor `claude-local`; Agent `codex-local` likewise with `codex-local`; a Grok row whose model is the local Grok model maps to the grok adapter with lineup vendor `grok-local`. Add the three names to `supportsVendor`. Keep the Agent field as the key (adj 155); this reading of the owner's answer is to be confirmed.
3. Environment: the launchers own the base URL and key (`agents/llmnode/docs/agents.md:22-60`). ork adds no URL setting and passes no key; it inherits the daemon environment. Nothing local goes in `projects.json` or `vendor_env`.
4. Caps and marks: one shared local pool of 2 slots across the three local vendors (one server, owner estimate 2 to 4 requests); each local vendor has its own out mark. Cloud and local marks are independent.
5. Reasoning and timeouts: check what `--effort` does under the launcher, since `claude-local` sets `CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL` itself and the server accepts low, medium and xhigh. Check that a reply of tens of seconds, and the 30 minute hung timer (`engine.DefaultHungAfter`), do not classify as a failure.
6. Fallback: classify an unreachable endpoint through the existing adapter classifiers as an error, so adj 156 moves to the next matrix row; if the classifiers do not do that, add the narrowest rule.
7. Update the matrix row r33 to the launcher Agent value with `slicer relay-roles`; local versus frontier stays a matrix row, with no separate ork setting. Update `docs/design.md`, `docs/boundaries.md` and `docs/state.md` to match.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- Open owner questions, to file with `adj ask` under `roles.local-model` with `--ref` this slice, each with a recommendation: (1) the Agent value for each local row (recommend the launcher names `claude-local` and `codex-local`, and Agent `Grok` with the local model for Grok); (2) the name of the local model in Grok's config; (3) one shared local cap of 2 or a cap per local vendor (recommend shared, one server). The owner answered the other questions on 2026-11-06 (see Implement); record them with `adj decide` only as the owner picks.
- Evidence from step 1 of Implement is in the handoff note.
- `go test ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `gofmt -l .`, `slicer check`, `adj lint`.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: - Branch and worktree per AGENTS.md; no commit until the owner approves.

sections.heading: Not in this slice
sections.body: No role defaults to local. No second local model at once. No Nemotron or 8-bit Qwen row (untested). Writing or changing the launchers and their key handling (the agents repo). Measuring local quality. A base URL or key setting in ork.
